messages:
maria: Quick Q — onboarding Acme POC. Need hosted API access for integration tests. Can we issue a scoped, short-lived API token (generate+embeddings) that expires in ~72h? Customer also wants IP allowlist to their CI IPs and a rotation ceremony. CC @devin (SE).

devin: Yes — we can do ephemeral tokens via console or a service-account with rotating creds. For speed, 72h ephemeral token is simplest. How many IPs to allowlist?

maria: They provided two static CI IPs + one corporate VPN exit: 203.0.113.10, 203.0.113.11, 198.51.100.22. POC window is 2 weeks. They want automated rotation every 48h and ability to manually rotate before demos.

ashley: Security note: for >72h we prefer service-account + KMS-backed secrets. Ephemeral tokens are OK for short POCs but require a ticket + justification. Audit logs for hosted tokens are captured in the console; we can bump retention to 90 days for enterprise questionnaires. Also need customer contact for incident communication.

maria: Understood. For this POC, stick with 72h ephemeral token and a documented rotation runbook. I'll add customer contact.

ops-bot: /create_poc_token helper — usage: `/create_poc_token <customer> <expiry_hours> <scopes> <ip_allowlist>` (admins only). Please include `poc/acme` in the request metadata.

devin: I'll create initial token now and record audit id. @sam — can you approve a service-account fallback if they push to longer-term?

sam: Approve fallback. FYI hosted tokens are not model-scoped; you can limit by scopes (generate, embeddings, rerank). If they need model pinning, pass model_version in requests or use Dedicated.

jordan: On the customer side I'll prepare a short README for CI env var rotation and demos.

ashley: Add to the security questionnaire: token revocation process (console + API), who to contact on exposure, retention window for logs, and whether the customer will accept our ephemeral token flow or requires SSO-backed service accounts.

maria: Customer contact is techlead@acme.test. I'll open the ticket with required fields and request the 72h token with the three IPs.

devin: Ran: `/create_poc_token acme 72 generate,embeddings 203.0.113.10,203.0.113.11,198.51.100.22`
```
Created token: ****REDACTED****
Expires: 72 hours
Audit: audit-2145000000-01
Console: https://console.redwood.ai/poc/acme/tokens/audit-2145000000-01
```

ops-bot: Token created by devin. Expires at +72h. Audit id: audit-2145000000-01. Token delivery performed via secure DM to maria and jordan.

maria: Sending token to customer via 2FA DM and adding rotation notes in the ticket. I'll author the runbook in Confluence and attach to the POC ticket.

jordan: I'll add a demo script and set a calendar reminder T-4h before token expiry for a manual rotate.

ashley: Can we test revocation quickly? Simulate a compromise: revoke and reprovision to validate the flow.

devin: Revoking now...

ops-bot: Token audit-2145000000-01 revoked by devin.

devin: Verified — calls now return 401. Reprovisioned new token with same scopes, different audit id.

sam: Add this sample to docs: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` and a short snippet for revocation via API.

maria: Thanks all — closing the loop on this thread. I will attach the security questionnaire answers and ticket id 2145000000 to the customer record.
